# Florence 1490 – Institutions, law & governance

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Written, published law code** [`written_law_code`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_law_code.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. City statutes (1415 redaction) plus Roman and canon law, in Latin, known to lawyers and notaries rather than citizens. Local: the Florentine Pandects (6th-century Digest manuscript in the Palazzo della Signoria); Arte dei Giudici e Notai.
- **Rule of law and separation of powers** [`rule_of_law`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rule_of_law.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Republican institutions (Signoria, councils) exist but are controlled by the Medici through patronage. Ideas of the mixed constitution are discussed by humanists.
- **Independent judges and judicial review** [`independent_judiciary_judicial_review`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/independent_judiciary_judicial_review.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Judges (podestà) are hired foreigners on short terms and audited on leaving, to keep them impartial. Political cases go to the Otto di Guardia, which obeys the regime. Local: Podestà (Bargello); Otto di Guardia.
- **Habeas corpus and fair trial** [`habeas_corpus_fair_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/habeas_corpus_fair_trial.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Procedure is inquisitorial: secret denunciations in boxes (tamburi), detention at the magistrates' will, torture to confess, exile without trial. Elsewhere: England: jury trial and the writ.
- **Representative government (elected assembly)** [`representative_government`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/representative_government.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Florentine councils vote on laws and taxes. Eligibility is restricted, and the Medici influence appointments. The Council of Seventy, created in 1480, concentrates power. Elsewhere: Venice: Great Council; England: Parliament; Castile and Aragon: Cortes.
- **Selection of officials by lot (sortition)** [`sortition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sortition.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The Signoria has two-month terms. The regime controls the electoral purses and can substitute selection by hand for a draw. Local: Palazzo della Signoria; accoppiatori.
- **Direct democracy (citizen assembly voting on laws)** [`citizen_assembly`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/citizen_assembly.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. A parlamento of citizens in the piazza is called only to approve emergency commissions (balìe); ordinary laws pass through restricted councils. Local: Palazzo della Signoria.
- **Secret ballot** [`secret_ballot`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secret_ballot.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Councils vote with black and white beans; secrecy is imperfect and votes are watched. Elsewhere: Venice: elaborate secret balloting for the Doge and offices.
- **Peaceful transfer of power and loyal opposition** [`peaceful_transfer_of_power`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/peaceful_transfer_of_power.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Civic offices rotate regularly. Medici influence passed within the family in 1464 and 1469. The Pazzi attack of 1478 failed to displace Lorenzo.
- **Written constitution** [`written_constitution`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_constitution.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Statutes describe the offices, but any special commission (balìa) called by a staged assembly can suspend them.
- **Federalism and subsidiarity** [`federalism_subsidiarity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/federalism_subsidiarity.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Florence rules Pisa, Arezzo, Pistoia and Volterra as subjects, and they resent it. Italy's states ally but would never share sovereignty. Elsewhere: Swiss Confederation; Hanseatic League.
- **Treaties, diplomacy and international law** [`international_law_sovereignty`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/international_law_sovereignty.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Resident ambassadors and written leagues are Italian inventions of this century. The Pope claims to arbitrate between kings, also over newly found lands. Local: Florentine chancery (Bartolomeo Scala); Otto di Pratica (foreign affairs). Elsewhere: Rome: papal bulls dividing discoveries (Aeterni regis 1481).
- **Secure property rights and land registry** [`property_rights_land_registry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/property_rights_land_registry.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Property is secured by notaries' deeds and listed in tax declarations (catasto, 1427 onward). No surveyed public register; exiles' property is confiscated. Local: Catasto officials; notarial archives.
- **Contracts, notaries and merchant courts** [`commercial_law_contract_enforcement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/commercial_law_contract_enforcement.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Florence's merchant court, notaries and account books as legal proof are among the best in Europe. Local: Tribunale della Mercanzia; Arte dei Giudici e Notai.
- **Patent law** [`patents`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/patents.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Venice has a patent statute since 1474. Florence grants occasional privileges (Brunelleschi got one for a boat in 1421). Guilds dislike monopolies held by outsiders. Elsewhere: Venice: patent statute of 1474.
- **Copyright for authors** [`copyright`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copyright.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Printers reprint freely. Venice has begun granting single privileges (to an author, Sabellico, in 1486); Florence grants none. Elsewhere: Venice: printing privileges.
- **Standard weights and measures** [`standard_weights_measures`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_weights_measures.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Each city has its own braccio, pound and bushel, checked by guild and commune within its walls. Merchants convert with handbooks. A common system threatens local privileges. Local: guild inspectors; Zecca (mint) assayers; merchant handbooks (pratiche di mercatura).
- **Census and registration of births and deaths** [`census_vital_registration`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/census_vital_registration.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The catasto lists households. San Giovanni's baptism registers survive from November 1450. The Grascia and the physicians' guild keep separate death registers. Local: Baptistery of San Giovanni registers; Libri dei morti; Catasto.
- **Public accounts, audit and budget** [`public_accounts_audit`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_accounts_audit.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. Officials are audited on leaving office and the public debt has double-entry books. The Medici regime moves public money for its own needs unseen. Local: Ufficiali del Monte; Camera del Comune.
- **Merit-based civil service (examinations)** [`merit_civil_service`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/merit_civil_service.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. Learning and writing skill matter for chancery appointments. Eligibility, patronage and selection by lot shape other offices. Local: Bartolomeo Scala (chancellor, a miller's son). Elsewhere: China: examination system.
- **Universal elementary schooling** [`universal_schooling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_schooling.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Reading masters and abacus schools serve urban families who can pay. Girls also learn at home or in convents. Access varies by wealth and location. Local: abacus schools; grammar masters.
- **University (self-governing body of teachers and students)** [`university`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/university.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Lorenzo moved law, medicine and theology to Pisa in 1473; Florence keeps the humanities (Greek, rhetoric). Teaching is commentary on set texts. Local: Studio of Pisa; Studio fiorentino (Poliziano, Chalcondyles until 1491). Elsewhere: Padua and Bologna (medicine, law).
- **Scientific society or academy** [`scientific_academy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_academy.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Ficino's correspondents and pupils exchange texts and discuss Plato. They offer contacts for a learned society, though there is no chartered Florentine Platonic academy. Local: Marsilio Ficino and his correspondents.
- **Organised industrial research laboratory** [`industrial_research_lab`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/industrial_research_lab.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Large workshops and the wool guild have money and skilled men but invest in proven work. A patron could fund a standing workshop of inventors. Local: Arte della Lana; Opera del Duomo. Elsewhere: Venice: the Arsenal.
- **Public library and museum** [`public_library_museum`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_library_museum.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. San Marco's library admits scholars and lends access to Greek and Latin manuscripts. Young sculptors can study antiquities in the Medici garden. Local: San Marco library; Medici sculpture garden near San Marco; Medici private library. Elsewhere: Rome: Vatican Library; Capitoline bronzes (1471); Cesena: Malatestiana.
- **Freedom of the press** [`free_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/free_press.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Printing is barely regulated yet. Innocent VIII's bull of 1487 demands prior censorship by bishops; it is little enforced. Rulers punish afterwards.
- **Abolition of slavery** [`abolition_of_slavery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_slavery.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Enslaved people work in Florentine households. Notarial records and merchants' links with Iberia offer evidence of the trade. Legal status varies with origin and circumstances. Local: slave-owning households; Ospedale degli Innocenti (many foundlings are slaves' children).
- **Women's legal rights and suffrage** [`women_rights_suffrage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/women_rights_suffrage.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Women have dowry and inheritance claims and can make wills. Statutes favour male heirs, and women are excluded from political office. Local: Alessandra Scala (Greek scholar); Monte delle Doti. Elsewhere: Venice: Cassandra Fedele.
- **Perpetual endowment (waqf, foundation, trust)** [`charitable_endowment_waqf`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charitable_endowment_waqf.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Hospitals, foundling home and confraternities live on endowed farms and houses; founding one earns salvation and honour. Local: Ospedale degli Innocenti; Santa Maria Nuova; Misericordia; Buonomini di San Martino.
- **Craft guilds and apprenticeship** [`guilds_apprenticeship`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/guilds_apprenticeship.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Seven major and fourteen minor guilds control training, quality and entry, and political rights. They block outsiders, new methods and women; wool workers may not organise. Local: Arte della Lana; Arte di Calimala; Arte della Seta; Arte dei Medici e Speziali.
- **Permanent public health authority** [`public_health_board`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_health_board.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Florence appoints temporary plague officials in epidemics; Milan and (since the 1480s) Venice have permanent offices. A permanent Florentine office would be a real advance. Local: Signoria; temporary plague officials. Elsewhere: Milan: permanent health office; Venice: Provveditori alla Sanità.
- **Fire brigade, civil police and building rules** [`fire_brigade_police_building_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fire_brigade_police_building_codes.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The Otto di Guardia and their constables keep order, a night curfew holds, and the commune keeps a small fire watch. The city is stone and tile; no pumps. Local: Otto di Guardia; Ufficiali di Torre.
- **Social insurance and poor relief** [`social_insurance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_insurance.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Guilds and confraternities aid sick members and widows; the state dowry fund is a savings scheme for fathers. Nothing is compulsory or covers labourers. Local: Monte delle Doti; confraternities; Buonomini di San Martino (the 'shamed poor').
- **Trade unions and collective bargaining** [`trade_unions_collective_bargaining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trade_unions_collective_bargaining.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Cloth workers are forbidden to assemble; the Ciompi rising of 1378 is the ruling class's nightmare. Proposing this is sedition.
